blurb: Fanout's public 2026 roadmap for LLM inference engineering — token generation and KV-cache math through serving, quantization, and capacity planning.

adaptedFrom.name: Fanout (Suraj Gaud)
adaptedFrom.note: Fanout publishes no open licence on its site; Sikhi University has Fanout's written permission to build this reading map. No roadmap text is reproduced here — the card opens the real page at fanout.sh. Fanout states the full course is still being assembled; this path links its public roadmap and course comparison, not a finished paid product.

modules.title: The 2026 roadmap
modules.objective: Read Fanout's public LLM inference engineering roadmap — from token generation and workload definition through weights, KV-cache math, continuous batching, PagedAttention, quantization, serving runtimes, distributed execution, benchmarking, and observability.
modules.teach: This sits a level above the AI School's own LLM Engineering and Infrastructure & Production phases: it is specifically the production-serving half of the stack, aimed at backend, ML, and platform engineers moving models from a demo to real traffic. As of this writing Fanout says the full course is still being assembled, so treat this as a roadmap and comparison to bookmark and revisit, not a finished paid course to buy today.
